body: @chuckjaz could you please take a look ?

It seems that the problem is that at the beginning the async pipe emits null.
See example http://plnkr.co/edit/XBcem9ozBeSxMn0aBuOm?p=preview
@CaselIT this is exactly why he uses `?.` operator

The issue is the assumption that generating an expression twice will generate the same expression producing the same value.  The generated code looks like:

``` js
var currVal_0 = jit_interpolate7(1,'Async value: ',
  ((valUnwrapper.unwrap(self._pipe_async_0.transform(self.context.observable)) == null)? 
    null: 
    valUnwrapper.unwrap(self._pipe_async_1.transform(self.context.observable)).value),'')
```

This observes two values coming from the pipe instead of just the first one. It checks the first for `null` then assumes the second will be non-null. The solution is to introduce a temporary storing the result of the first invocation. The would result in code like,

``` js
var tmp_0;
var currVal_0 = jit_interpolate7(1,'Async value: ',
    ((tmp_0 = valUnwrapper.unwrap(self._pipe_async_0.transform(self.context.observable)) == null)?
      null: 
      tmp_0.value),'')
```

I will work on introducing the temporary variable.

issue.title: fix(compiler): Generate temporary variables for guarded expressions

**What is the current behavior?** (You can also link to an open issue here)

When generating code for null guarded expressions (using the `?.` operator) pipes and method calls are called twice. This can lead to incorrect behavior for pipes where the pipe might change value for the second invocation.

**What is the new behavior?**

Pipes and method calls are now only evaluated once and the result is saved in a temporary variable.

issue.title: RC5 changes - ? operator and async
issue.body:

```
[x?] bug report
[ ] feature request
[ ] support request => Please do not submit support request here, instead see https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#question
```

**Previous behavior**
Using RC4, the following would work...
`*ngIf="(searchResults | async)?.length > 0"`
or
`*ngIf="(searchResults | async)?.length == 0"`

**Current behavior**
RC5 throws 
`TypeError: Cannot read property 'length' of null`

This syntax does work in RC5
`*ngIf="((searchResults | async) || []).length > 0"`
and
`*ngIf="((searchResults | async) || {}).length == 0"`

**What is the expected behavior?**
The original RC4 behavior seems more intuitive, especially when checking `.length == 0` since it did not evaluate until the observable returned.

**Please tell us about your environment:**
- **Angular version:** 2.0.0-rc.5
- **Browser:** [Chrome ] 
- **Language:** [TypeScript 1.9]
